text: Path copying, persistent arrays, static range k-th.

A persistent (可持久化) segment tree keeps every old version. A point update only changes the log n nodes on one root-to-leaf path, so copy just those nodes and point the copies at the old, unchanged children. Each version is one root; versions share everything else.
Memory: n nodes for the first tree, plus about log₂ n + 1 new nodes per update.
Children can no longer be 2p and 2p + 1: store ls[p] and rs[p] explicitly and hand out node numbers with ++tot.

"Version i is based on version v" is just root[i] = modify(root[v], …) . A query never copies anything, so it can share the root. This is a persistent array: any old version can be read or branched from (P3919 is the template).

Build a value segment tree (权值线段树 , 第6章) for every prefix: version i = version i − 1 with a[i] inserted. The counts are additive, so cnt in version r minus cnt in version l − 1 is the value tree of a[l..r].
Walk both trees down together, exactly like the k-th query of 6.3.
Node 0 is the empty tree: ls[0] = rs[0] = cnt[0] = 0, so version 0 needs no build at all, and missing children read as count 0.

O((n + m) log n) time, about n · (log₂ n + 1) nodes (P3834). The same "prefix versions subtracted" idea answers: how many values in a[l..r] lie in [x, y]; the best xor with a value in a range (P3293 美味 , bits walked from the top as in the 0-1 trie of 第7章); and with versions over time instead of positions, queries at a moment (P3168 任务查询系统).

Size the pools for all versions: n log n nodes for the prefix trees, plus log n per update in the persistent array. Recursion depth is only log n, but forgetting to copy ls / rs / val into the new node silently drops half of the old tree.

title: 树状数组套权值线段树

text: Range k-th with point changes in O(log² n).

A persistent tree is built once; it cannot take a point change at position i, because every later prefix version would change too. Fix: replace "prefix versions" by a Fenwick tree whose cells are value segment trees (树状数组套权值线段树). Cell i holds the value tree of the block (i − lowbit(i), i] of positions.

Changing a[i] updates the log n cells that contain i, each in log n steps. A query for a[l..r] collects the log n cells of prefix r and of prefix l − 1, and walks all of them down at once, adding and subtracting their left- child counts: O(log² n) per operation.

Question about a[l..r] k-th / rank Array changes? Tool many queries, no changes no persistent segment tree (8.1), O(log n) queries mixed with point changes yes Fenwick tree of value trees (8.2), O(log² n) only answers needed, all known in advance yes offline: CDQ divide and conquer / overall binary search (选读)

The value trees are created on demand (动态开点): upd(int &p, …) makes a node only when a count first reaches it, so the total is O((n + m) log² n) nodes instead of n separate full trees. All values, including those that appear only in changes, are read first and discretised together (P2617).

Same structure, other questions: rank of x, predecessor, successor in a range (P3380 树套树); inversions while deleting elements, counting pairs with a Fenwick tree over positions and value trees inside (P3157 动态逆序对); three-dimensional partial order, sort by the first key and use a Fenwick tree of value trees for the other two (P3810).

Memory is the danger: with n = 10⁵ the pool needs tens of millions of ints. Count nodes as (initial values + 2 × changes) × log₂ n × log₂ K before choosing the array size, and prefer the offline methods when the limit is tight.
